h1: The 6 Best Smart Plugs for Lamps of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Smart Plugs for Lamps: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 smart plugs for lamps compared on ecosystem support, footprint, hub needs, Matter and multi-pack value.
summary: The Kasa Smart Plug Ultra Mini is the best lamp plug, working with Alexa and Google in a slim body that leaves the neighboring socket free. The Linkind Matter plug is the choice if you run Apple Home, the Amazon Smart Plug is the easiest for Echo owners, and the Kasa 4-pack is the one for a whole house of lamps.
intro: A lamp is the easiest thing in the house to automate, and the one where the wrong smart plug is most irritating. A fat plug blocks the second outlet. A plug without a physical button leaves you stranded when the Wi-Fi drops. And a lamp with a dimmer bulb or a touch base can confuse a plug that only switches power.

We ranked six smart plugs from the listings: ecosystem support, hub requirements, body size, setup, scheduling and pack size. All six switch power on and off, so none can dim a bulb. They suit lamps with a physical switch left in the on position, or a lamp that turns on when power returns.

products.name: Kasa Smart Plug Ultra Mini 15A
products.verdict: A slim 15A plug with timers and countdowns that works with Alexa and Google Home.
products.description:
The Kasa Ultra Mini is a 15A plug on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi with timer and countdown functions and support for both Alexa and Google Home. The mini body is the headline for lamps, since it sits against the wall without covering the second socket.

It ranks first because it works across both major assistants and stays small. It beats the standard Kasa HS103P4 on footprint, though the HS103P4 adds a touch actuator and a four-pack. Against the Amazon plugs it gains Google Home support.

Buy it if your lamp shares an outlet. Skip it if you use Apple Home, which this plug does not list, and you have a 5GHz-only network.
pros: Slim body frees the second socket
Works with Alexa and Google Home
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a slim lamp plug for either assistant.

products.name: Linkind Matter Smart Plug
products.verdict: Matter support across Apple Home, Alexa and Google Home, with control over the local network.
products.description:
The Linkind is a Matter smart plug that works with Apple Home, Alexa, Siri and Google Home, and runs on the local network with remote app control.

It ranks second because Matter matters most in a mixed household. One plug works across assistants, and local control means the lamp still switches when the internet is out. It trails the Kasa Ultra Mini on body size and brand track record.

Buy it if you have iPhones and an Echo in the same house. Skip it if one assistant is enough and you want the cheapest plug.

keySpecs.label: Platforms
keySpecs.value: Apple Home, Alexa, Siri, Google Home

cons: Matter setup is fussier at first
products.idealFor: Mixed households with Apple, Alexa and Google devices.

products.name: Amazon Smart Plug
products.verdict: The Alexa-native plug with guided setup and a physical on switch.
products.description:
The Amazon Smart Plug works with Alexa, needs no hub and walks you through setup in the Alexa app. A physical switch on the device turns it on without the app.

It ranks third because setup is the smoothest in this group for an Echo household, but it works only with Alexa. It sits below the Linkind and Kasa because those cover more assistants. It beats the Amazon Basics plug on the physical button.

Buy it if you live inside the Alexa app. Skip it if you might ever add Google or Apple devices.
products.idealFor: Echo households wanting the easiest setup.
products.skipIf: You use Google Home or Apple Home.

products.name: Kasa Smart Plug HS103P4
products.verdict: Four plugs with a touch actuator and support for Alexa and Google Home.
products.description:
The Kasa HS103P4 comes in a four-pack with a touch actuator, Alexa and Google Home support, and no hub requirement. You get a plug for every lamp in the living room, bedroom and den.

It ranks fourth because the body is larger than the Ultra Mini, which can block the second socket on a tight wall outlet. The four-pack lowers cost per plug, and the touch button gives control when the app is slow.

Buy it if you plan to automate several lamps. Skip it if your outlets are crowded and each plug must stay slim.
products.idealFor: Homes with lamps in several rooms.

products.name: Amazon Basics Smart Plug
products.verdict: A compact single-socket plug with built-in scheduling for Alexa users.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics plug works only with Alexa, fits one socket, includes scheduling and has a zero-touch setup option that links it to your Echo.

It ranks fifth because it costs more than the Amazon Smart Plug, in the $25-50 range, yet loses the physical on switch. Its advantage is the slim footprint that leaves neighboring sockets free, and the zero-touch linking.

Buy it if you want the slimmest Alexa plug. Skip it if you want a manual button or Google support.
cons: Costs more than the Amazon Smart Plug
products.idealFor: Alexa users who want a slim plug.

products.name: GHome Smart Plug
products.verdict: An entry-level plug with timers for a single lamp, on Bluetooth or Wi-Fi.
products.description:
The GHome offers Bluetooth or Wi-Fi connection, Alexa and Google Assistant support, remote app control and timers.

It ranks last because the listing is thin on load rating, size and hub details, and the brand is less proven than Kasa. It suits a single lamp where the plug does a simple on and off.

Buy it if you want a basic plug for one lamp. Skip it if you want a documented load rating or Matter support.
products.idealFor: People who want a plain plug for one lamp.

whatMatters.detail: Smart plugs speak to Alexa, Google Home or Apple Home, and some speak to all. Matter plugs work across assistants from one device. On a listing, read the compatibility line carefully, since Alexa only plugs will not work with Google or Apple. Mixed households should favor Matter, which reduces the chance of buying twice.

A bulky plug can cover the second wall socket, forcing you to waste an outlet. A slim plug sits flat against the wall. Check the listing for a mini or compact body, and photos beside a double outlet. Two plugs side by side only fit when both bodies are slim.

Many plugs, including the Kasa Ultra Mini, run only on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. If your router combines bands, setup can fail. Check the listing for the Wi-Fi band and use the 2.4GHz network during pairing. If your router merges bands, split the network briefly during pairing.

A button on the plug works when the internet or app fails. The Amazon Smart Plug and Kasa HS103P4 list one. Look for a touch actuator or on switch on the listing, since a lamp that cannot turn on is frustrating. It also gives a fallback when a guest cannot use the app.

The rating tells you how much power the plug can switch, such as 15A. A lamp draws far less, so the number matters most if you reuse the plug elsewhere. Check the rating if you may plug in a heater or fan later. Lamps with built-in dimmers should stay on their own switch.

faq.q: Can a smart plug dim my lamp?
faq.a: No. These plugs only switch power on and off. Use the Kasa Ultra Mini or Linkind to schedule a lamp, and buy a smart bulb if you want dimming. That keeps a nightstand lamp on a schedule without extra gear.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying an Alexa-only plug and later adding Google or Apple devices. The Amazon Smart Plug and Amazon Basics plug work only with Alexa, while the Linkind spans Apple Home, Alexa and Google. Smart bulbs cost more but handle dimming and color.

faq.q: Is the Linkind worth it over the Kasa Ultra Mini?
faq.a: If you use Apple Home, yes. The Linkind adds Matter and local control, while the Kasa Ultra Mini has a smaller body and a longer track record. Pairing takes a couple of minutes per plug.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Plug it in, open the app and follow pairing. For the Kasa Ultra Mini, use your 2.4GHz network. The Amazon Smart Plug walks you through it in the Alexa app. Matter plugs can pair to several assistants at once.
No. The Amazon Smart Plug, Kasa HS103P4 and Linkind all list no hub requirement. They connect to your router directly. Hubs only matter for older Zigbee gear.

faq.q: Can I use one on a touch lamp?
faq.a: Often not well. A touch lamp can turn off when power is cut, then stay off when power returns. Test a lamp with a physical switch left on first. Lamps with a mechanical switch are the safest bet.

finalTake: The Kasa Smart Plug Ultra Mini is the best lamp plug because it is slim, works with Alexa and Google and runs timers and countdowns. Pick the Linkind if you use Apple Home, the Amazon Smart Plug for the easiest Echo setup, and the Kasa four-pack for lamps in several rooms.
